status_caveat: ENVIRONMENT-CONDITIONAL. As of synoi-conformance 0645377 the runner shells to the prebuilt b1-harness binary when it is present and reports b2-v1..v7 PASS/FAIL from live harness output (runner-SHIPPED, confirmed 2026-06-20 this environment, binary present). In a toolchain-less environment the binary is absent and every b2 vector reports NOT-EXECUTABLE-IN-RUNNER and v1-v7 stay PARTIAL; no fake pass is ever emitted. v8-v11 are DESIGN/PAPER B3-loader placeholders that NEVER pass in the runner regardless of toolchain. The top-level status stays PARTIAL because runner-SHIPPED is not portable: it holds only where the Rust toolchain has built the harness. v1-v7 evidence in run_evidence.harness_stdout is real captured Rust-harness output. Re-tagged 2026-06-20 by Auditor (iteration-9 sweep): runner-shelling honest, environment-conditional qualifier added.

vectors.name: b2-v8-gate-consult-axes-1-2-3-7-before-render
vectors.description: DESIGN PLACEHOLDER -- B3 loader-integration work, gated on B0 sign-off. Per ADR_005 Section 5 per-invocation sequence: before calling render-panel the shell/loader calls gate.consult-gate(bundle_oid, principal, context). Gate must return a signed GateDecision citing axes_consulted (at minimum 1:integrity, 2:policy, 3:entitlement, 7:time), axes_denied, reason_cdros, expires_at. On allow, the invocation proceeds. On deny, the shell emits a signed denial receipt and renders shell-owned denial chrome without calling the bundle export.
vectors.blocked_on: B0 sign-off (ADR_005 Section 12: Architect, Security on Sec 4+5, Auditor, Joshua); B3 shell/loader implementation
vectors.will_pass_when: Shell/loader wires gate.consult-gate per ADR_005 Sec 5; gate axis aggregator emits a signed GateDecision; harness adds a deny-path vector confirming export is NOT called on deny.

vectors.name: b2-v9-hybrid-signature-verify-on-load
vectors.description: DESIGN PLACEHOLDER -- B3 loader-integration work. Per ADR_005 Sec 1, the bundle CDRO carries signature { ed25519, ml_dsa_65, signed_at }. The loader must verify the hybrid signature before instantiating the bytecode. This is NOT a WIT export but a loader precondition. Vectors needed: (a) valid hybrid sig passes, (b) tampered bytecode_oid fails load, (c) revoked signer fails load (axis 1 integrity check).
vectors.blocked_on: B0 sign-off; signed CDRO packaging (capbundle/1 schema); synoi-verify path wired into the loader
vectors.will_pass_when: Loader verifies hybrid sig at load time; harness can supply a signed bundle and a tampered bundle and observe accept/reject.

vectors.name: b2-v11-shell-emitted-invocation-receipt

After the export returns, the shell hashes the result and signs a render-completion receipt. Both receipts are emitted to the receipt log and verify at the public verifier path. This is shell-side work, not bundle-side.

first_slice_dod_assessment.floor_note: ADR_009 Sec 3 floor is 3 vectors per declared export. render-panel has 3 PARTIAL (v1/v2/v3). handle-receipt has 3 PARTIAL (v4/v5/v6). run-onboarding has 1 PARTIAL (v7) -- boundary/second-call variant is that run-onboarding is stateless; calling it twice would produce the same result; v7 covers the only distinct observable behavior. PARTIAL = Rust-harness-captured, not runner-executed; the ADR_009 floor is met at the harness level but is not runner-backed until the runner shells to/links the Wasmtime binary.
first_slice_dod_assessment.run-onboarding-second-call-note: A second call to run-onboarding produces identical output (completed=true, payload=[]). No additional observable state is exercised. This is a first-slice limitation: real onboarding steps (e.g., entitlement enrollment, key-custody setup) are B3 scope. The second-call variant collapses into v7 for this slice.
